A FUGHETTTA FOR CLARA
by Tina Rankin
In a little farmhouse
sits a little girl
who wishes she were a boy.
She eats plain toast
and waits for her brother
to bring home blue eggs
or anything at all
that isn't black.
She sits by the window
and wishes she were a crow
with ragged wings
or really any bird
with a dagger beak
that can peck
into a lemon tart.
She likes the way
the sharp filling
cuts through the rich cream.
It makes her teeth ache,
and the ache makes her think.
That's why she's made a resolution
to eat a tart every day
until she can turn the world
a proper, dazzling yellow.
Ripe peaches. Flaming daffodils.
A flock of goldfinches
Against a wild blue sky.
She'd like a head start
before he gets back
with the trees.
Can you see her shuffle
across the field
with tarts in her pocket
leaving creamy footprints
as she heads for the woods?

3-4 tbsp cold water
For the filling:
3 free-range eggs, preferably organic
2 free-range egg yolks
170g caster sugar
Finely-grated zest of 1 lemon
Juice of 1 lemon – around 60ml

110g caster sugar

For the pastry, heat the oven to 200°C, fan 180°C, gas 6. Put the flour and salt into a food processor. Add the butter and pulse until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Add the water a tablespoon at a time and pulse until the dough comes together. Tip the dough out of the processor and press into a circle with your hands. Wrap in cling film and chill for at least 30 minutes. Make the filling. Put the eggs, egg yolks, sugar, lemon zest and lemon juice into a food processor and pulse a few times to combine. Tip into a large bowl and whisk until smooth and thick – it should drop off the whisk in thick ribbons. Roll the pastry out to fit a 23cm loose-bottomed tart tin and press in. Trim off the excess pastry, prick the base with a fork and chill until needed. Spoon the filling into the pastry case and smooth the top. Put on a baking tray to catch any spills and bake for 30-40 minutes until just set. The filling will wobble a little but shouldn’t be runny. Meanwhile, make the topping. Put the egg whites into a large, clean, dry bowl and whisk until they form soft peaks. Gradually add the sugar and whisk until the mixture is thick and glossy. Remove the tart from the oven and pile the meringue on top. Make swirls with a knife and sprinkle over some extra sugar if you like. Bake for a further 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp. The filling should be set. Serve with some extra fresh lemon if you like.<|endoftext|>
